newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares tumble on poor first-half results.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares tumble on poor first-half results.

text.p: An onslaught of disappointing first-half profit announcements this week has sent shares prices reeling on the Bombay Stock Exchange and shaken investors, traders said on Wednesday.
"People are looking at the numbers and getting worried. In some cases, earnings are coming out even worse than expected," said Keshav Sanghi at James Capel B&K sales in Hong Kong.
Leading Indian firms Grasim Industries, Hindalco Industries, Century Textiles, Titan Industries and Essar Steel have all announced lower net profits for the first half of 1996/97 (April-March).
The stock prices of these firms have taken a pounding as a result.

Shares of Century Textiles -- which said on Monday its net profit plunged 66.7 percent to 341.8 million rupees ($9.6 million) due to the high cost of borrowing money and higher tax provisions -- slid 4.5 percent to 2,220 rupees on Wednesday.
Century shares had plummeted 10 percent on Tuesday.
At 0835 GMT on Wednesday, Bombay's benchmark stock index was trading 66.92 points or 2.13 percent lower at 3072.41.
"There are some unpleasant surprises still left," said Rupa Bose, regional analyst and India strategist at Paribas Capital Markets in Singapore.
"Analysts have been over-optimistic. I don't think they recognised how difficult operating conditions had become for the companies in the second half of last year," Bose said.
She said tight money conditions and infrastructure problems such as power cuts and rail-transport delays at the end of 1995 had bled companies of much of their profit in the first half.

"Most companies have been hit by interest costs which were very high. The results obviously reflect the slowdown that we have been seeing," said Rajashekar Iyer, head of research at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
Diversified firm Grasim said on Tuesday its first-half net profit fell 12.6 percent to 1.47 billion rupees. It said output of viscose staple fibre was hit by power shortages and monsoon delays.
Grasim shares fell 14 rupees or 3.7 percent to 365 rupees in afternoon trade on Wednesday.
"The market will only move up if interest rates fall and investors start focusing on 1997/98. If cyclical commodity stocks turn around, that also would help," Capel B&K's Sanghi said.
Kotak's Iyer said recent slight improvement in some global commodity prices including steel could begin to cheer sentiment.

"We think the market still hasn't finished factoring in the bad news. It could go down further in the next couple of months on earnings disappointments, more depressing economic statistics and more negative political headlines," Bose said.
"We think the (index) could go below 3,000 quite easily."
